The current sanitizer only matched a bare `` opener, so attributed tags fell through to the generic HTML stripper and arrived at the channel as raw text. ## Why This Change Was Made Updated the regex in `src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.ts` to accept optional attributes on the opening `` tag (`/]*)?>(.*?)<\/code>/gi`), matching the existing treatment of `]*>` and `]*>` in the same function. Added a focused unit test covering `class` and multiple attributes. ## User Impact Users on Telegram, iMessage, IRC, Google Chat, WhatsApp, and other channels that rely on `sanitizeForPlainText` will now see inline code rendered with backticks even when the model produces attributed `` tags, improving readability of code snippets in channel messages. ## Evidence ### Reproduced behavior on current `main` The bug is deterministic from the source: `/(.*?)<\/code>/gi` does not match ``, so the tag is stripped by the generic `HTML_TAG_RE` remover. ### After-fix runtime proof (public SDK export) The patched helper is the same `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound` export that Telegram, iMessage, and other channel adapters import at runtime: ```bash $ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx -e "import { sanitizeForPlainText } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound'; console.log('attributed:', sanitizeForPlainText('foo()')); console.log('plain:', sanitizeForPlainText('bar()'));" attributed: `foo()` plain: `bar()` ``` ### Unit tests ```bash $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts ✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts (29 tests) 17ms ``` ### CI note Rebased onto `upstream/main` (`dfa31af0d4`) to resolve the `CHANGELOG.md does not contain a release section for 2026.7.2` failure in the QA Smoke CI build. target.title: feat(media): allow host-read vCard (.vcf) files
target.body:
Closes #97062

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users sending a local `.vcf` (vCard) contact file via the `MEDIA:` directive or `message(media=...)` would see:

```
Host-local media sends only allow buffer-verified images, audio, video, PDF, and Office documents (got text/vcard)
```


The only workaround was to manually base64-encode every file as `message(buffer=...)`, which is unnecessary friction for a standard RFC 6350 plain-text format.

## Why This Change Was Made

`file-type` (the MIME sniffing library OpenClaw uses) already recognizes vCard content and returns `text/vcard`. The missing piece was that `text/vcard` was not present in the host-read document allowlist. The fix adds it:

- **`packages/media-core/src/mime.ts`**: `EXT_BY_MIME` — enables `mimeTypeFromFilePath` to resolve `.vcf` → `text/vcard`, and `extensionForMime` to resolve `text/vcard` → `.vcf`
- **`src/media/web-media.ts`**: `HOST_READ_ALLOWED_DOCUMENT_MIMES` — allows the sniffed MIME to pass through `assertHostReadMediaAllowed`

`HOST_READ_TEXT_PLAIN_ALIASES` is intentionally unchanged. Unlike CSV, Markdown, TXT, JSON, and YAML (which have no magic bytes), `file-type` already detects vCard content, so `text/vcard` takes the standard sniffed-MIME path, not the plain-text alias fallback.

This is a narrowly scoped fix. Only the host-read send path is changed; `input_file` MIME lists, file-transfer plugin, UI MIME maps, and docs remain untouched.

### Security boundary hardening (added in review)

Both Codex review and a source review flagged that `file-type` only reads the first ~1MB prefix. A buffer starting with `BEGIN:VCARD\n` sniffs as `text/vcard`, but the remaining bytes could be arbitrary binary data. The sniffed-document allowlist path previously returned immediately on match without full-buffer validation for any MIME type.

The fix adds a guard in `assertHostReadMediaAllowed`: when a sniffed document MIME starts with `text/`, the full buffer must pass `isValidatedHostReadText` (printable character ratio > 0.95) before the file is accepted. This closes the prefix-only detection window for `text/vcard` and any future `text/*` MIME additions.

## User Impact

Users can send local `.vcf` contact files through `MEDIA:` directives and `message(media=...)` without workarounds. The file loads as a `text/vcard` document and can be delivered normally to channels that support contact sharing.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Using the patched `loadWebMedia` (the internal API behind `MEDIA:` / `message(media=...)`) to verify the fix end-to-end:

**Setup:**
```bash
# Create a standard .vcf contact file
cat > /tmp/proof.vcf << EOF
BEGIN:VCARD
VERSION:3.0
FN:Test Contact
TEL:+1-555-0000
END:VCARD
EOF
```

**Test 1 — valid .vcf accepted:**
```
$ npx tsx proof-vcf.mjs

--- Test 1: valid .vcf via loadWebMedia ---
kind: document
contentType: text/vcard
buffer.length: 66
fileName: proof.vcf
STATUS: PASS
```

**Test 2 — malicious .vcf (BEGIN:VCARD header + binary tail) rejected:**
```
--- Test 2: malicious .vcf with binary tail ---
error: Host-local text/vcard media sends require buffer-verified plain-text content.
STATUS: PASS (correctly rejected)
```

### Tests

All tests pass (`pnpm test` runs two Vitest shards):

**`packages/media-core/src/mime.test.ts`** — 100/100 passed

New test cases added alongside existing YAML entries in each parameterized suite:

| describe | Test | Verifies |
|----------|------|----------|
| `mime detection` | `maps vCard files to text/vcard` | `detectMime({ filePath: "/tmp/contact.vcf" })` returns `"text/vcard"` |
| `mimeTypeFromFilePath` | `maps contact.vcf` | `mimeTypeFromFilePath("contact.vcf")` returns `"text/vcard"` |
| `extensionForMime` | `maps text/vcard` | `extensionForMime("text/vcard")` returns `".vcf"` |
| `extensionForMime` | `maps Text/VCard` | `extensionForMime("Text/VCard")` returns `".vcf"` (case-insensitive normalisation) |
| `mediaKindFromMime` | `classifies text/vcard` | `mediaKindFromMime("text/vcard")` returns `"document"` |

**`src/media/web-media.test.ts`** — 78/78 passed (one new regression test added during review)

| Test | Input | Asserts |
|------|-------|---------|
| `allows host-read vCard files` | `contact.vcf` with valid VCF content (BEGIN:VCARD / END:VCARD) | Returns `kind: "document"`, `contentType: "text/vcard"` |
| `rejects vCard files with a valid header and binary tail` | `evil.vcf` with `BEGIN:VCARD\n` prefix + 9000 bytes non-NUL binary tail | Throws `"path-not-allowed"` — regression guard against prefix-only file-type detection |
| `rejects opaque non-NUL binary data disguised as vCard` | `opaque.vcf` with non-printable binary content (non-NUL bytes only) | Throws `"path-not-allowed"` |

### Format and lint

```
$ oxfmt --check All matched files use the correct format.

$ oxlint Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

---

This PR is AI-assisted. Analysis, implementation, and testing were performed using opencode with human review by the author.

target.title: fix(agents): keep scp stderr tail UTF-16 safe
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where SCP stderr tail truncation can produce invalid Unicode when sandbox filenames contain emoji or other supplementary-plane characters.

`appendScpStderrTail()` caps raw `child.stderr` output with `combined.slice(-maxChars)` before the text is surfaced in `throw new Error(\`scp failed (${code}): ${stderr.trim()}\`)`. SCP stderr is unfiltered (unlike treemap label sanitization), so paths like `📊report.csv` can land on a UTF-16 surrogate boundary and leave a lone high surrogate in operator/agent-visible errors.

**Concrete example:** `appendScpStderrTail("prefix", "🤖tail", 5)` with the old slice could keep `U+D83D` without its low half; the thrown error then carries malformed Unicode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw tail slice with `sliceUtf16Safe(combined, Math.max(0, combined.length - maxChars))` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, matching the established tail-truncation pattern in `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts` (#103757) and `src/node-host/invoke.ts`. Ring-buffer size and SCP behavior are unchanged; only the truncation boundary is surrogate-safe.

## User Impact

**Before:** SCP failures for media staging can surface replacement glyphs or invalid Unicode in agent/operator error text when stderr mentions emoji filenames near the tail cap.

**After:** SCP stderr tails remain well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts` — `appendScpStderrTail` uses `sliceUtf16Safe` for the tail cap
- `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts` — shared surrogate backoff helper
- Helper regression: `src/auto-reply/reply.stage-sandbox-media.scp-remote-path.test.ts`
- Caller-path regression: `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts` (`testing.scpFile` mocked `spawn` stderr bisect case)
- Live subprocess proof: production `testing.scpFile` and `stageSandboxMedia` exercised with the real `/usr/bin/scp` binary (no `spawn` mock)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** SCP stderr tail truncation no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when an emoji filename crosses the tail cap before the error is thrown to the agent/operator.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `stageSandboxMedia` remote attachment staging → `scpFile` spawns `scp` → `child.stderr` chunks → `appendScpStderrTail` ring buffer → `finish(new Error(\`scp failed (${code}): ${stderr.trim()}\`))` on non-zero exit.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; real OpenSSH `scp` subprocess via production `testing.scpFile`, plus `stageSandboxMedia` remote-cache path with emoji attachment filename and captured runtime log line.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`; provider/channel constraints N/A because this is sandbox media staging stderr handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node 22, branch `fix/scp-stderr-tail-utf16` @ `e8222a145cc`, real `/usr/bin/scp` against `git@github.com` (public host; no operator credentials printed).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx -e "
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { testing } from './src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts';
const tmp = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'scp-live-proof-'));
try {
  await testing.scpFile('git@github.com', '/tmp/🤖missing.jpg', path.join(tmp, 'download'));
} catch (error) {
  console.log(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
}
"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply.stage-sandbox-media.scp-remote-path.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts -t "UTF-16|scp stderr tail|scpFile" --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx …testing.scpFile('git@github.com', '/tmp/🤖missing.jpg', …)
scp failed (255): subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed

$ OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 node --import tsx -e "
…stageSandboxMedia({ remoteMediaMode: 'cache', ctx.MediaRemoteHost: 'git@github.com', MediaPath: '/Users/demo/Library/Messages/Attachments/ab/cd/📊report.jpg', … })
"
Failed to stage inbound media path /Users/demo/Library/Messages/Attachments/ab/cd/📊report.jpg: Error: scp failed (255): subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed
unpaired_surrogates=false

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs … -t "UTF-16|scp stderr tail|scpFile" --reporter=verbose
 ✓ keeps scp stderr tail UTF-16 safe when the boundary bisects an emoji
 ✓ surfaces UTF-16 safe scp stderr when transfer fails with emoji at tail boundary

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  5 passed | 5 skipped (10)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Live production `scpFile` retained real `scp` stderr through `appendScpStderrTail` and surfaced a well-formed `scp failed (255): …` message with `unpaired_surrogates=false`. `stageSandboxMedia` reached the same production path for an emoji remote attachment filename and logged a well-formed failure without splitting surrogate pairs. Supplemental mocked caller regression still proves the 16,384-code-unit emoji low-surrogate tail boundary that natural short `scp` stderr does not reach in this environment.
- **What was not tested:** Live `scp` against a reachable operator sandbox host with >16,384 code units of stderr before the emoji filename error; full gateway/iMessage inbound delivery roundtrip.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gateway restart loop where the same interrupted main session can be accepted for automatic recovery on every boot. Supervisor backoff does not make the session healthy, so attempts separated by minutes or hours must still consume one durable recovery budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-session restart recovery now has one canonical persisted fuse: `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery`.

- `automaticAttempts` counts accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recoveries since the last non-aborted run settlement on the same session.
- The first three recoveries may dispatch. An exhausted row is tombstoned before a fourth dispatch, with no elapsed-time expiry.
- A recovery attempt is reserved under the session-store writer lock before Gateway dispatch. The reservation is rolled back only when the request is known not to have been accepted; post-dispatch transport uncertainty keeps the attempt charged.
- Gateway admission revalidates the exact session and reservation identity before accepting a recovery run.
- Foreground admissions use a lifecycle-generation-scoped token set to fence concurrent recovery scans. Each admission releases only its own token on unaccepted, undispatched, or settled paths, so overlapping foreground requests cannot expose or permanently suppress recovery.
- A run that reaches normal session-store settlement without `aborted` clears `mainRestartRecovery`, including background progress that does not touch interaction/activity metadata. Session replacement and reset also clear it.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle suppression only; it is not used to derive the durable retry budget.
- Subagent orphan recovery retains its separate policy: two attempts in the existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Tombstone state is committed before the best-effort operator notice is sent, so a stale or failed notification cannot race the quarantine decision.
- Doctor reports wedged main and subagent sessions and can clear only stale `abortedLastRun` flags that conflict with an existing tombstone; it does not re-enable automatic recovery.
- Session-store cache identity uses nanosecond `ctime`/`mtime` plus size so same-size writes inside one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

This adds no public config, environment variable, wire protocol, provider route, or plugin API.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three accepted or acceptance-uncertain recovery attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use `/new` or reset.

Healthy progress restores the full budget. The fuse does not expire merely because time passes.

## Evidence

Current branch:

```text
base: upstream/main@99ddde87262
head: 2408915c9ce
```

Current-head local static proof:

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main
```

The final autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings. Local runtime tests were intentionally not run because this is contributor/fork code and the repository requires secretless fork CI or sanitized AWS Crabbox; the available sanitized AWS environment had no IMDS role.

Exact-head CI for `2408915c9ce`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29142465164

- Passed the Gateway test shard, build, lint, production types, test types, guards, dependency checks, and the other PR-relevant jobs.
- The run has two inherited failures that reproduce unchanged on the already-merged #104210: stale `docs/docs_map.md` output for `Resident local STT`, and the missing `core/doctor/local-audio-acceleration` contribution in `doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`. They are outside this PR's diff and were not folded into this branch.

Focused regression coverage in the branch includes:

- cumulative attempts across slow restart intervals and tombstone-before-fourth behavior;
- pre-dispatch rollback versus post-dispatch acceptance uncertainty;
- exact reservation identity and stale scan rejection;
- concurrent foreground owner tokens, per-owner release, and settlement cleanup;
- successful/background progress reset and session reset/replacement cleanup;
- Doctor reporting/repair and main/subagent ownership separation;
- session-store cache invalidation for same-size rapid rewrites.

Prior real Telegram Desktop behavior proof remains applicable to the user-visible recovery path:

- Workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010
- Artifact bundle: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010/artifacts/8106022765
- Manifest: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/index.json

The baseline replayed the exhausted recovery turn before handling a fresh message. The candidate quarantined the exhausted row and handled the fresh Telegram message without another automatic resume.

target.title: fix(codex): preserve UTF-16 pairs in tool output delta truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex streaming tool output display renders a corrupted glyph ("�") when a non-BMP character (emoji like 😀) straddles the 8,000-character progress-message truncation boundary. The raw `.slice(0, remainingChars)` on the emitted delta cuts at a UTF-16 code-unit boundary — when `remainingChars` lands on the HIGH surrogate of a surrogate pair, the truncated progress message carries a dangling `\uD83D` that corrupts the rendered output in the chat transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` is already imported on line 29 and used at two other call sites in the same file (lines 3413, 3435) for the 10,000-char transcript-output path. This single progress-message call site at line 1447 was missed during the original import. The fix reuses the canonical helper — no new abstraction, no new import.

## User Impact

Streaming tool output in the Codex chat UI no longer renders a corrupted replacement character when model-generated tool output contains emoji characters near the 8,000-character progress limit. ASCII-only output is unaffected.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A non-BMP character (emoji surrogate pair) that straddles the `TOOL_PROGRESS_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` (8,000) boundary in the Codex event projector's `handleOutputDelta` progress-message path must not produce a lone surrogate in the emitted transcript text.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, x64, linux, OpenClaw checkout at `2d0d06d3f1`

### Evidence after fix — standalone runtime proof

A standalone Node.js script (`proof-codex-projector-runtime.mts`) imports the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` class directly from `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts`, drives it through `handleNotification` with `verboseLevel: "full"`, and prints the actual `onToolResult` callback text. This is NOT a test framework — it is a real process executing the production code path.

```
── [Case 1] remainingChars=1, delta=😀hello ──
onToolResult calls: 3
[call 0] len=32 lone=false
🛠️ `show emoji.txt (workspace)`
---
[call 1] len=8019 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
aaaa...aaaa
```
---
[call 2] len=37 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
...(truncated)...
```
---
── [Case 2] remainingChars=2, delta=x😀y ──
onToolResult calls: 3
[call 0] len=33 lone=false
🛠️ `show emoji2.txt (workspace)`
---
[call 1] len=8018 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
aaaa...aaaa
```
---
[call 2] len=39 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
x
...(truncated)...
```
---

=== RUNTIME PROOF COMPLETE ===
node=v22.22.0
No lone surrogates in any emitted progress text.
Fix confirmed: truncateUtf16Safe in production projector.
```

**Case 1** — remainingChars=1, delta starts with 😀: `truncateUtf16Safe` detects the HIGH surrogate at position 0 and backs off, producing an empty chunk. The progress message is `...(truncated)...` — clean, no surrogate bytes.

**Case 2** — remainingChars=2, delta="x😀y": `truncateUtf16Safe` cuts at position 1 (the 'x'), backs off before the emoji at positions 1-2. The progress message is `x\n...(truncated)...` — clean, no surrogate bytes.

### Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced)

Same standalone script, same environment. `event-projector.ts` reverted to `origin/main` (`.slice(0, remainingChars)`) — the script picks up the old code via tsx on-the-fly compilation:

```
── [Case 1] remainingChars=1, delta=😀hello ──
[call 2] len=39 lone=true              ← BUG: lone surrogate detected!
🛠️ Bash
```txt
�                                     ← U+D83D HIGH surrogate, corrupted glyph
...(truncated)...
```
---
── [Case 2] remainingChars=2, delta=x😀y ──
[call 2] len=40 lone=true              ← BUG: lone surrogate detected!
🛠️ Bash
```txt
x�                                    ← "x" + U+D83D HIGH surrogate
...(truncated)...
```
---
```

**Case 1 old code:** `.slice(0, 1)` on `"😀hello"` cuts after the HIGH surrogate at position 0, producing `"\uD83D"` → the markdown-fenced progress message renders `�` (corrupted glyph).

**Case 2 old code:** `.slice(0, 2)` on `"x😀y"` cuts after the HIGH surrogate at position 1, producing `"x\uD83D"` → the progress message renders `x�`.

Restoring the fix — same script, same process — all calls show `lone=false`, clean text.

### Quantitative summary

| Metric | Old `.slice()` | Fix `truncateUtf16Safe` |
|--------|---------------|------------------------|
| Case 1 lone surrogates | 1 (`U+D83D`) | 0 |
| Case 2 lone surrogates | 1 (`U+D83D`) | 0 |
| Case 1 emitted chars at cap | 8,000 (includes split surrogate) | 7,999 (backed off) |
| Case 2 emitted chars at cap | 8,000 (includes split surrogate) | 7,999 (backed off) |

### What was not tested

- **Real Codex app-server process:** The projector is driven through its public `handleNotification` API with manually constructed events, not a live Codex Rust binary. The event shapes match the upstream Codex protocol (`item/commandExecution/outputDelta`), but a live session with model-generated emoji output at the exact 8,000-char boundary was not reproduced.
- **macOS / Windows:** Proof was collected on Linux x64 only. The fix is platform-independent (pure string manipulation in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts`).
- **Non-bash tools:** Only `commandExecution` (tool name `"bash"`) was tested. Other tool types (`fileChange`, `mcpToolCall`) share the same `handleOutputDelta` entry point and the same `truncateUtf16Safe` call.

## Evidence

**Change surface:** 1 file, 1 line — `delta.slice(0, remainingChars)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(delta, remainingChars)` at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts:1447`.

| Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Source | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Tests | 1 | 122 | 0 | +122 |
| **Total** | **2** | **123** | **1** | **+122** |

Test-to-fix ratio: 122:1 test lines per production line changed.

**Runtime proof:** `proof-codex-projector-runtime.mts` — standalone Node.js script (NOT a test framework) that imports the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` class, drives it with `verboseLevel: "full"` and `onToolResult` callback, and prints the actual emitted text. Full positive and negative control output above in Real behavior proof.

**Vitest regression:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — new test "keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap" (122 lines) covers 3 UTF-16 edge cases at the 8,000-char boundary. Adjacent UTF-16 tests pass (no regression on the 10,000-char transcript path).

**Canonical helper contract:** `truncateUtf16Safe` in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts:44` retains the existing maximum-code-unit semantics but backs off when the truncation boundary falls between a valid HIGH and LOW surrogate. Already used at lines 3413 and 3435 in the same file.

**No competing PRs:** `gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open "event-projector AND (utf16 OR surrogate OR truncateUtf16Safe)"` returns no open PRs covering the same call site.

target.title: fix(feishu): drive info finds files past the first page
target.body:
Closes #93928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users running `feishu_drive info` received `File not found` for files that were not present on the first page of the root drive listing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Drive info now queries Feishu's metadata API directly by file token and type instead of searching a single root-list response. Shortcut lookups retain the existing root-list behavior because the metadata endpoint does not support the shortcut type, and installations without the metadata scope fall back to the legacy lookup for compatibility.

## User Impact

Users can retrieve metadata for supported files regardless of the containing shared folder or root-list page. Existing read-only installations continue to support root-level info lookups, while direct lookups require `drive:drive.metadata:readonly` or the full `drive:drive` scope.

target.body:
Closes #103758

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where LINE groups configured with `requireMention: true` could not require a mention before non-text messages (image/video/audio/file) reached the agent. Any photo, video, voice clip, or file posted in such a group was always processed, regardless of whether the bot was actually mentioned, because LINE's Messaging API never attaches mention metadata to non-text messages and the mention-gate logic could not account for that.

Fixes an issue where operators of mention-gated LINE groups would see the bot react to every image/video/audio/file dropped in the chat, even when nobody addressed the bot, when they expected the same "must be mentioned" behavior that already applies to text messages (per #34438 / #35847).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two new **opt-in** LINE group config fields — `requireMentionForNonText` and `pendingMediaLimit` — so operators can explicitly turn on mention gating for non-text messages without changing default behavior for anyone else. Because LINE never reports a mention on the non-text message itself, a bounded per-group pending-media queue (default limit 3) retains the most recent skipped media until a later message in the same group is mentioned and fully processed, at which point the queued media is attached to that turn and the queue is cleared. This lets a user post a photo, then follow up with `@bot look at this`, and have the photo still reach the agent.

A prior attempt at the opt-in flag alone (#68197) went stale without merging and did not include the retention queue, which meant skipped media was simply dropped forever once a group opted in — this PR keeps the same opt-in, default-false posture that maintainers asked for on #68197, and adds the missing retention piece on top.

## User Impact

LINE operators can now set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.groups.<groupId>.requireMentionForNonText: true` (alongside `requireMention: true`) to require an `@mention` before non-text messages reach the agent, matching the existing text-message behavior. Skipped media isn't lost — up to `pendingMediaLimit` (default 3) recent items are retained per group and delivered alongside the next mentioned message. Existing configs are unaffected since both fields default to off/unset.

## Evidence

`pnpm test:extension line` — 26 test files, **313 tests passing** (up from 307 on `main`; +6 in `bot-handlers.test.ts`, +2 in `config-schema.test.ts`):

```

- unmentioned non-text message is skipped when `requireMentionForNonText` is set (and the pre-existing "allows non-text through by default" test is preserved unchanged, proving no default-behavior change);
- pending-queue eviction bounded by `pendingMediaLimit` (oldest dropped first);
- queued media flushed into `allMedia`/`processMessage` context on a later mentioned message, then the queue is cleared;
- default `pendingMediaLimit` of 3 when unset;
- schema acceptance of both new fields and rejection of non-positive `pendingMediaLimit`.

target.title: fix(extensions/anthropic): preserve migrated model entries when inherited keys shadow converted refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where adopting Claude CLI auth could silently drop a model's custom settings (aliases, parameters, etc.) or throw when the global `Object.prototype` contains an inherited property matching the converted Anthropic model ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteModelEntryMap` used `converted in next` to decide whether to copy a legacy `claude-cli/*` entry to its Anthropic equivalent, and then assigned with `next[converted] = value`. The `in` operator follows the prototype chain, and the assignment can throw or invoke an inherited setter when `Object.prototype` is polluted. The migration could therefore skip the copy, delete the original `claude-cli/*` key, and lose the user's model configuration.

The change now:
- checks own-property membership with `Object.hasOwn`;
- writes migrated and seeded entries with `Object.defineProperty` so they become own properties even when `Object.prototype` has a getter-only accessor, non-writable data descriptor, or setter.

This applies the same own-entry invariant that #103373 adds to the Anthropic API-key default-allowlist seeding path.

## User Impact

Users whose runtime has a polluted `Object.prototype` no longer lose per-model aliases or other metadata, and no longer see migration throws, when adopting Claude CLI-backed Anthropic refs.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```bash
pnpm test extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts --run
```

Result: 19 passed.

The regression suite covers four Object.prototype descriptor collisions and fails against the parent commit:
- inherited writable data descriptor;
- inherited non-writable data descriptor (throws before the fix);
- inherited getter-only accessor (throws before the fix);
- inherited setter accessor (entry becomes undefined before the fix, setter is not invoked after).

### Type / lint

```bash
pnpm tsgo:extensions        # exit 0
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.ts
```

Both pass.

### Live migration proof

Controlled run with an `Object.prototype` getter-only accessor shadowing the converted ref:

```text
=== Claude CLI auth adoption migration proof ===
Scenario: Object.prototype has a getter-only accessor for the converted ref.
Migrated entry: {
  "alias": "Work Opus",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" }
}
Entry is own property: true
Alias preserved: true
Parameters preserved: true
```

The alias and `temperature` parameter survive migration, and the resulting entry is an own property of `models` rather than the inherited accessor value.

## Release Note

- Anthropic: preserve migrated model aliases and parameters when inherited prototype keys shadow converted Claude CLI refs.

Related: #103373

target.title: fix(agent-tools): add request timeout to remote media fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent-side image, image-generation, and PDF tools fetch remote media through `loadWebMedia` / `loadWebMediaRaw` with only a body-idle gap guard (`readIdleTimeoutMs`). A remote endpoint that accepts the TCP connection but withholds response headers forever leaves the fetch open indefinitely — `readIdleTimeoutMs` only governs gaps between body chunks, never the pre-header stall. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through the three agent-tool call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end through the three agent-tool call sites.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/agents/tools/media-tool-shared.ts` — new export `REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000` next to the existing `REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts:1042`, `image-generate-tool.ts:675`, `pdf-tool.ts:487` — on the `isHttpUrl` branch, the spread becomes `{ readIdleTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, responseHeaderTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS }`.
- `src/agents/tools/{image,image-generate,pdf}-tool.test.ts` — the prior `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000` assertions added by the previous version of this branch are removed (the canonical seam is now exercised end-to-end via the `loadWebMedia` forwarding layer; per-tool assertions would be redundant).
- `proof-103209-image-tool-layer.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end through `loadWebMedia` (the entrypoint image-tool/image-generate-tool/pdf-tool invoke), real stalled HTTP server, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape.

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for image, image-generation, and PDF tool calls against stalled remote endpoints.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (120s for agent-tools) continues to bound chunk gaps.
- Users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. This matches the existing 15-minute ceiling from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`); the trade-off has already been accepted by maintainers on that merge.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (image-tool entrypoint `loadWebMedia`, real HTTP server, real fetch, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape)

Local fallback run (Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-103209-image-tool-layer.mts
[proof] stalled HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:35937
[proof] calling loadWebMedia (the entrypoint image-tool/image-generate-tool/pdf-tool invoke)
[proof] with responseHeaderTimeoutMs=1000ms (production uses 15*60_000)
[proof] this exercises the canonical seam from PR #103020:
[proof]   loadWebMedia -> readRemoteMediaBuffer -> fetchGuardedMediaResponse
[proof]   -> fetchWithSsrFGuard -> buildTimeoutAbortSignal (response header deadline)
[proof]   -> globalThis.fetch
[proof] elapsed: 1160ms
[proof] surfaced error.name: MediaFetchError
[proof] surfaced error.code: fetch_failed
[proof] surfaced error.message: Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:35937/never-responds.png: request timed out
[proof] surfaced error.cause.name: TimeoutError
[proof] surfaced error.cause.message: request timed out
[proof] result: responseHeaderTimeoutMs fired through real production path
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:35937/never-responds.png",
  "responseHeaderTimeoutMs": 1000,
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "error",
    "name": "MediaFetchError",
    "code": "fetch_failed",
    "message": "Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:35937/never-responds.png: request timed out",
    "causeName": "TimeoutError",
    "causeMessage": "request timed out",
    "elapsedMs": 1160
  },
  "passed": true
}
```

Key observations:
- **1160ms elapsed** (vs 1000ms `responseHeaderTimeoutMs`): the canonical seam fires at the deadline.
- **Surfaced error shape**: `MediaFetchError { code: "fetch_failed", cause: TimeoutError("request timed out") }` — the exact error the image tool's `execute` function throws when the underlying fetch stalls. The agent runtime will surface a clean "request timed out" error to the caller instead of hanging.

### Repository test (forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs through the public seam)

The forwarding test ("forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer") lives on the companion branch #103206 in `src/media/web-media.test.ts`. Both branches share the same `WebMediaOptions` / `loadWebMediaInternal` forwarding code (this branch carries it for standalone typecheck; #103206 is the canonical owner of the seam), so the test exercises the same code path that image-tool / image-generate-tool / pdf-tool call into.

Focused suite runs (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  180 passed (180)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)
```

### Canonical precedents

- **PR #103020 / merge `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`** — `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` at `src/media/fetch.ts:82`; the canonical seam.
- **PR #103266 / merge `541c9f0bf01712d81d5217eb2a5c15d05686259d`** — canonical 15-minute bounded-media ceiling from `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`. This PR reuses the same ceiling on the narrower header-only deadline.
- **Telegram precedent** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.ts:356` already uses `TELEGRAM_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`. This PR's constant name mirrors that pattern.

## Coordination with #103206

With the canonical seam now on `origin/main`, both this PR and #103206 independently use that seam — they no longer duplicate each other and either can land in any order. No cross-repo stacking required. The forwarding test on #103206 covers the same `WebMediaOptions` → `loadWebMediaInternal` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer` path that this branch's three agent-tool call sites invoke. After #103206 lands, this branch can drop its duplicate `src/media/web-media.ts` forwarding changes (the seam becomes part of `main`).


## Post-review updates (2026-07-11)

ClawSweeper re-review (2026-07-11 03:39 UTC) identified one P1 finding:

### Covered video_generate

`video_generate` also loads reference assets through `loadWebMedia` but was omitted from the deadline rollout. Added `responseHeaderTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS` to both the sandbox and non-sandbox `loadWebMedia` calls in `src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.ts:633-642`.

Added `applies the shared response-header deadline when loading remote reference assets` in `src/agents/tools/video-generate-tool.test.ts`. It mocks `loadWebMedia` and asserts the call receives the canonical 15-minute header deadline. Verified by temporarily removing the deadline from `video-generate-tool.ts` — the test then fails because `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` is `undefined`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users completing onboarding through the remote wizard could have Gateway service installation begin before they acknowledged an installation warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway install-plan warnings are collected synchronously, then displayed and awaited in order before service installation starts. This preserves the install planner's synchronous warning contract while respecting the wizard prompter's asynchronous interaction contract.

## User Impact

Onboarding users now see and acknowledge Gateway installation warnings before OpenClaw installs the service, including when the wizard is driven through the Gateway API.

## What Problem This Solves

PR #88082 added `step-3.7-flash` to both direct StepFun catalogs (`stepfun` and `stepfun-plan`) but left the default model on `step-3.5-flash`. New onboarding runs and catalog defaults still select the older Step 3.5 model instead of the current flagship.

`STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` is the single source for both `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_REF` and `STEPFUN_PLAN_DEFAULT_MODEL_REF`. Those refs drive `onboard.ts` `primaryModelRef` and each auth method's `defaultModel`, so flipping the one id repoints both surfaces at `step-3.7-flash` with no other runtime wiring.

## User Impact

- Fresh StepFun onboarding (standard and Step Plan) now defaults to `stepfun/step-3.7-flash` / `stepfun-plan/step-3.7-flash`.
- Existing installs that pinned a model explicitly are unaffected; the change only moves the default for new setups.
- `step-3.5-flash` and `step-3.5-flash-2603` remain selectable.

## Evidence

- `extensions/stepfun/provider-catalog.ts`: `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` now `step-3.7-flash`.
- Updated `extensions/stepfun/index.test.ts` default-ref expectations; docs default/alternate wording and config examples updated.
- Local proof (Codex worktree fallback):

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` / `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe takes down the codex sandbox exec server.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`. Terminal notifications and backend finalization stay owned by the existing `child.once("close")` handler, so the process is never reported closed while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; a broken stderr pipe must not kill a healthy process — logged via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the exec server. Stdout failures terminate the managed process through the normal close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

**Realistic-stream regression** (`processes.stream-errors.test.ts`): `spawn` is mocked to return a child whose `stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin` are real `PassThrough` streams, driven through the production `startProcess` entry point. This exercises the real close path, including `finalizeProcess()` calling `stdin.destroy()` and `finalizeExec`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What the tests assert (after fix):**

1. **Stdout error → kill, then finalize via close:**
   - `managed.failure` is set; `child.kill("SIGTERM")` is called; `managed.closed` stays `false` and `finalizeExec` has NOT run yet (the error handler does not finalize).
   - After the real `close` event: `managed.closed` becomes `true`, `finalizeExec` runs exactly once with `status: "failed"`, and notifications are ordered `process/exited` before `process/closed`.
2. **Stderr error → warn only:** `embeddedAgentLog.warn` is called, `child.kill` is never called, the process stays alive, and `finalizeExec` does not run.

**Note on the prior revision:** the earlier fake child's `stdin` only implemented `end()`, so `finalizeProcess()`'s `stdin.destroy()` threw a `TypeError` that the close path swallowed — `finalizeExec` silently never ran even though the test passed. The `PassThrough` streams fix that: `finalizeExec` is now actually reached and asserted, so the finalization lifecycle is proven end-to-end.

**Static checks:** `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

**What was not tested:** a live OS-level pipe failure (requires resource exhaustion). The error path itself is exercised exactly — the production handlers registered by `startProcess` receive real stream `error` events and the real close/finalize lifecycle runs to completion.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts` — 2/2 passed
- `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text

```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status

Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
